findings.title: Unbound R55 aborts before K1 and bypasses completion cleanup
findings.counterexample: With the documented invocation and no inherited R55, set -u at L48, the sole root assignment R56 at L49, and expansion of $R55 at L169 cause an unbound-variable exit before enclose runs; the watchdog has already started at L157-162, and only TERM (not EXIT) has a completion trap. [Driver L48-49,L124,L157-169](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L48)
findings.consequence: k cannot produce the promised six-control result; N2 can see exit 1 from nounset rather than its intended injected assertion, but its required ONE-STRIKE/1-of-6 predicates then fail. A live watchdog/sleeper can be left after the top-level k shell exits. [Driver L169,L289-293](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L169)
findings.smallest_correction: Bind K1 to the frozen successor lane rather than ambient R55; preserve expected-negative discrimination and ensure abnormal driver termination enters bounded owner cleanup.

findings.title: Both inner-manifest pipelines can inventory their temporary output
findings.counterexample: Runner L316 and driver L102 redirect xargs output to SHA256SUMS.tmp without excluding that filename from find. In the permitted schedule where that pipeline member opens its redirection before find scans the directory, find includes ./SHA256SUMS.tmp; if hashing succeeds, mv renames it away and the final manifest names a nonexistent input, while rejection by the hash utility instead makes the intended positive publication fail. [Runner L316](../../s2-v56/run-composition-r56-v5.6-when-granted.sh#L316) [Driver L102](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L102)
findings.consequence: Runner outer verification hashes the inner manifest's bytes, not its entries, so it does not catch this before an otherwise-zero exit; the driver later checks the runner inner manifest and strikes, whereas its own result manifest is never reverified before publication_status=ok. This is a source scheduling counterexample, not an observed runtime failure. [Runner L318-329](../../s2-v56/run-composition-r56-v5.6-when-granted.sh#L318) [Driver L103-106,L142](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L103)
findings.smallest_correction: Exclude all publication temporaries or place them outside the inventoried tree; check the completed inner manifest before certifying immutable successful publication.

findings.title: Ack gating improves startup but registration failure and pending acquisition remain uncovered
counterexamples: Driver record writes and CURRENT publication at L65/L81 are unchecked; a data-block ENOSPC can make nonempty registry writes fail while creation of the zero-length ack still succeeds. L82 then permits workload exec despite neither durable ownership record nor watchdog authority being present. [Driver L58,L65,L76-87](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L58)

A TERM handled after runner spawn L207-208 but before STEP_PID assignment L209 reaches halt with an empty PID/group registry; the already published leader and its ack-wait sleeper are outside OWNED_PAT and can survive a claimed REAP ok/normal cleanup handoff. No workload exec is alleged here: lack of ack blocks it, but does not prove the child has been reaped. The driver similarly has no pending-enclosure adoption in on_cancel before L81 registration. [Runner L128,L150-184,L194,L207-210](../../s2-v56/run-composition-r56-v5.6-when-granted.sh#L128) [Driver L78-82,L115-124](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L78)
findings.smallest_correction: Require successful recoverable registration/current publication before ack; latch interruption through spawn/adoption and resolve the pending published child or explicitly preserve uncertainty as unsafe handoff. Extend only the affected startup seams to enclosures and cleanup clients.

findings.scope: Current signal authority and watchdog ownership; prior A-03/B-03
findings.title: Watchdog stop races sleeper replacement; historical PID imports can regain authority
counterexamples: stop_watchdog reads wd.sleeper once before killing the watchdog. It can read the first, already-exited sleeper, then the watchdog starts/publishes its second sleeper at L159, then stop kills only the shell and the old sampled PID. The second sleeper is outside OWNED/PAT and the census still examines only the sampled PID, so census_after=[empty] can omit a live child. The same publication gap exists at initial sleeper creation. [Driver L93-98,L157-162](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L93)

record_from_run imports every historical spawned PID from completed step logs at L69, including a K8 child already killed by the runner; if that numeric PID is reused before import/owned_cleanup, kill -0 and pruning retain the replacement and TERM/KILL target it. Dropping dead records after a later observation does not prevent this reacquisition from history; no current generation is bound. This is a specific reuse schedule, not a claim that reuse occurred. [Driver L66-75,L108-113,L250-256](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L66)
findings.positive_boundary: The previous newest-historical-pgid watchdog lookup is removed: CURRENT is now written on adoption and cleared on observed-empty retirement, and dead plain records can be pruned. These narrow changes are real but do not establish all-current ownership. [Driver L73-90,L156](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L73)
findings.smallest_correction: Stop/reap all watchdog-owned children under a closed spawn/stop handoff; retire authority without reacquiring historical numeric IDs as current ownership. Add deterministic transition/cancellation and retired-identity discriminators.

findings.scope: Cleanup, publication and total completion; prior A-02/A-03/A-05
findings.title: Bounded hashing is not bounded completion; final publication still admits a zero failure
counterexamples: After the nominal bounded TERM/KILL refusal, runner L257 still unconditionally waits for the unconfirmed cleanup child, even if it remains alive after KILL (for example blocked I/O). The deadline is not checked by that wait; CLEANUP_LEAK is set only afterwards. Driver refusal L85-87 has the same unconditional-wait tail. [Runner L250-259](../../s2-v56/run-composition-r56-v5.6-when-granted.sh#L250) [Driver L84-87](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L84)

Only the inner hash pipeline is enclosed. Runner receipt/outer-hash/reverification/final publication at L321-328 remain outside the timeout; driver stops its watchdog at L115 before final census and publication, checks elapsed time before publication at L119, then has an unenclosed receipt/stdout tail. A blocked write/read there has no total deadline; even a delayed successful driver receipt crossing BUDGET can still return 0 because there is no post-publication elapsed check. [Runner L316-329](../../s2-v56/run-composition-r56-v5.6-when-granted.sh#L316) [Driver L99-121](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L99)

After otherwise successful receipt/outer publication, failure writing PUBLICATION.txt (for example ENOSPC at that final write) is explicitly ignored at runner L327, leaving FINAL=0 and stdout status=ok. This is a required output of Request11 and a required successor predicate in the driver. [Runner L324-329](../../s2-v56/run-composition-r56-v5.6-when-granted.sh#L324) [Driver L140-141](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L140) [Request11 L17](../../s2-v56/PROOF_REQUEST_11.md#L17)
findings.smallest_correction: Bound/refuse unreaped-child waits and the complete cleanup/publication tail, reserve failure reporting, check the final required write, and classify the actual exit after all publication outcomes; retain first-failure and distinct cleanup registers.

findings.scope: neg2 control safety and claimed discrimination
findings.title: N4/N6 controllers lack cancellation cleanup; N5/N7 do not close all claimed seams
findings.counterexample: TERM to the outer driver during N4 or N6 enters finish but never reaches the normal-only DECOY/HOLDER cleanup. N4's caller-group sleep is deliberately absent from OWNED/PAT and can survive a reported empty handoff; N6's separate flock/sleep group is also unrecorded and can retain the private lock until its 40-second sleep ends. Keeping a decoy unowned by the tested cleanup must not make it unowned by its controller's cancellation path. [Driver L115-124,L325-339,L367-375](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L115)
discrimination_limits: N4b uses a fixed four-second timeout and checks final=143, not that TERM reached step40: an earlier interrupted step with clean cleanup can satisfy these predicates without the stated sleeping-composition scenario. [Driver L331-334](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L331)

N5a is a useful deterministic publication-failure seam, and N5b checks the published/unadopted seam and no harness output; neither covers pre-PID assignment or failed driver registration. N5b's controller also sends TERM after its polling loop expires without requiring that the seam was actually seen. [Driver L342-362](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L342)

N6 infers its holder's lock ownership after sleep 0.3 and treats any failed nonblocking flock as that owner, rather than a holder-ready acknowledgement. N7's ordinary sleep exits on first TERM; removing the watchdog KILL and driver-cancellation branches would leave its required TERM/current/empty-census assertions satisfiable. Thus N7 is not escalation or total-cancellation proof. [Driver L313-319,L367-382](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L313)
findings.smallest_correction: Add a separate controller-resource registry/finally path, acknowledge the intended negative-control state, refuse timed-out synchronization, and exercise the affected cancellation/escalation seam rather than infer it from a first-TERM success.

findings.scope: Control grant payload and real-proof caller
findings.title: Request commands mask raw status and the allowed write set disagrees with execution
counterexamples: Every Request10 command ends with echo, so in the ordinary non-errexit caller a failed set is followed by successful echo and then the next set; the displayed STOP instruction is not implemented. Request11 has the same masking even when manifest verification fails before the runner starts. [Request10 L20-31](../../s2-v56/CONTROL_REQUEST_10.md#L20) [Request11 L12-16](../../s2-v56/PROOF_REQUEST_11.md#L12)

Request10 authorizes predecessor output writes only for new2, but new1 actually invokes K7pre and K8pre while new2 runs K10. The private lock is also opened/created under controls-proposed/stubs, outside the request's enumerated write directories. This is grant scope, not cosmetic control naming. [Request10 L25-35](../../s2-v56/CONTROL_REQUEST_10.md#L25) [Driver L227-266](../../s2-v56/controls-proposed/run-controls-v56.sh#L227) [Runner L99,L336](../../s2-v56/run-composition-r56-v5.6-when-granted.sh#L99)
findings.smallest_correction: Use an explicit status-preserving, stop-on-first-nonzero caller and align set-to-workload/output/lock authorization with the actual frozen driver; keep control versus real execution grants separate.
